newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Buyers say Taiwan soy shipments to come from U.S..
newsitem.headline: Buyers say Taiwan soy shipments to come from U.S..

text.p: Taiwan soybean buyers confirmed on Tuesday that two Taiwan-bound shipments would be from the United States because supplier Continental Grain did not want to buy from South America.
"Continental Grain decided to use U.S. soybeans over cost considerations," a buyer at Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association's Kaohsiung division told Reuters.
The U.S. Agriculture Department said on Monday exporters had switched a sale of 108,000 tonnes of soybeans to Taiwan to U.S. origin.
USDA requires U.S. exporters to report commodity sales of 100,000 tonnes or more.

On March 7 Taiwan's Kaohsiung division bought a 54,000-tonne shipment from Continental under an "optional origin" contract that allowed Taiwan to procure the soybeans from either the United States or South America.

The division had wanted South American soybeans to be at least US$5 cheaper than U.S. beans per tonne, but Continental was willing to sell South American soybeans only at a discount of US$2 per tonne, the buyer said.
Separately, the Taichung division of the Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association on March 11 bought a 54,000-tonne shipment of soybeans from Continental Grain with similar shipment schedules.
Both divisions' shipments were slated for delivery from late April to early May, traders said.
